expected_root_cause.statement: Release 2.14.1 changed ORDER_TAX_RATE_BPS from 825 to 8.25. compute_totals parses the value with int() on every POST /v1/orders, which raises ValueError, and the unhandled exception becomes HTTP 500.
expected_root_cause.why_rollout_continued: GET /healthz does not read the setting, so new instances passed their health gate.

evidence_tiers.source: disposable environment run; old value passes, new value fails
metrics.csv: v2_14_1 about 60% HTTP 500, v2_14_0 stays at baseline, every minute 14:02-14:31
config-diff.txt plus logs.ndjson stack and trace.json app.config.read: ORDER_TAX_RATE_BPS is read at the failing frame, and the error quotes 8.25
release.json code_changed=false. The trace points at the line that reads the changed value, which counts as tier 3
logs.ndjson: ValueError first at 14:02:04; only TimeoutError before it
metrics.csv: overall HTTP 500 about 3%, 15%, 30% at rollout 5%, 25%, 50%
first failure 4 seconds after rollout start

contradicting_evidence_example.treatment: Must be cited and resolved, not ignored. Hypothesis: orders-db caused the errors.
ruled_out_because: It is one reconnect on an old-version instance, and that request returned 200.
It came after the first failure.
Old-version HTTP 500 rate stays at baseline.
The changed value is not a database setting; the pool and timeout settings are unchanged context lines.
The trace shows SELECT cart succeeded.
contradicting_evidence_example.would_contradict: Version 2.14.0 instances failing with the same ValueError, or the error beginning before 14:02:00. Either leaves the contradiction unresolved, so the result drops to low and inconclusive.

hypotheses_to_weigh.statement: The changed config value breaks the order handler

hypotheses_to_weigh.verdict: ruled_out: known signature, unchanged rate, version 2.14.0 only

root_cause_wording: ORDER_TAX_RATE_BPS set to a non-integer value
Tax rate written as a percentage in a setting that expects basis points
Config cfg-42 breaks tax calculation on the order path
actions: release_rollback to 2.14.0: acceptable but high-impact, two approvers (ADR-49)
not_acceptable: Naming orders-db or the payment gateway as the cause
Citing the commit message as proof of intent

expected_escalation.severity: Proposed sev2; the incident lead confirms. Treated as high-impact until confirmed (ADR-49).
expected_escalation.approval: One approver after sev2 is confirmed. synthetic-engineer-a may not be the sole approver.
